players.product: High-speed copper / fiber-optic / power interconnects + CPO connectivity (incl. CommScope)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Craig Lampo, Q2 2026 by segment: Communications Solutions sales $5.4 billion, up 85% in US dollars and 42% organically (segment operating margin 33.6%); Harsh Environment Solutions $1.9 billion, up 28% in US dollars and 22% organically (segment operating margin 30.1%); Interconnect and Sensor Systems $1.5 billion, up 17% in US dollars and 13% organically (segment operating margin 21%). GAAP operating margin 29.5%; GAAP diluted EPS $1.37, up 59%; adjusted effective tax rate 27% versus 24.5% a year earlier; operating cash flow $1.6 billion (88% of net income) and free cash flow $1.2 billion (68% of net income); Q2 EBITDA $3 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: Communications Solutions $5.4B (+85%, +42% organic); Harsh Environment $1.9B (+28%); Interconnect and Sensor Systems $1.5B (+17%); FCF $1.2B

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Adam Norwitt on Q2 end markets and the Q3 outlook versus Q2: defense 8% of sales, up 37% in US dollars and 24% organically, Q3 expected to increase in the low double-digit range; commercial air 4%, up 22% (21% organically) on higher aircraft production and next-generation content, Q3 expected up modestly; industrial 20%, up 56% in US dollars and 18% organically (CommScope's building connectivity added; double-digit growth in all three geographies), Q3 expected roughly at the same elevated levels; automotive 10%, up 9% (6% organically) with a pickup in demand for vehicles with electrified drivetrains, Q3 expected to remain at Q2 levels; communications networks 11%, up 55% in US dollars on CommScope but down 6% organically on demand moderations from network operators and wireless equipment manufacturers (CommScope itself grew year over year there), Q3 expected to decline in the mid-teens; mobile devices 4%, up 17% (14% organically) in smartphones, laptops and wearables, Q3 expected up roughly in the 20% range 'as we participate in the beginnings of a variety of new program launches for our customers.'
quarterly_data.figure: Defense 8% (+24% organic); industrial 20% (+18% organic); automotive 10% (+6% organic); communications networks 11% (Q3 down mid-teens); mobile devices 4% (Q3 up ~20%)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Craig Lampo: CommScope 'achieved just a bit over $1.2 billion here in the second quarter in sales.' CEO Adam Norwitt: CommScope is growing across its business, in IT datacom (AI applications), communications networks and the industrial / building connectivity market; it sells its products through distribution into 'I don't know, 150, 180 different countries around the world', and Amphenol looks forward to using those distributor relationships for other Amphenol interconnect and sensor products in construction and building connectivity.

CEO Adam Norwitt: completed two acquisitions in Q2. El.Com Srl (Leno, Italy; annual sales of approximately $150 million) makes complex interconnect solutions and high-voltage cable assemblies for the industrial, defense and commercial aerospace markets and adds value-add interconnect capabilities for European industrial customers. Wilder Technologies (Washington State; annual sales of approximately $15 million) is a key supplier to Amphenol of high-performance test and measurement solutions for its high-speed interconnect applications for the IT datacom market.
quarterly_data.figure: El.Com ~$150M annual sales; Wilder ~$15M annual sales

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Adam Norwitt on the optics base: besides CommScope (whose IT datacom business is 'really around AI and around optics'), Amphenol already had 'a fiber optics business of significance before, both a passive optical interconnect business as well as an active optics business'; today it has 'a very strong high-speed copper business', a 'significantly scaled' optics business and 'a leadership position in power interconnect for AI.' On power electronics (asked about inverters and DC-DC converters): 'to the extent that we do anything there, it's pretty modest'; getting into 'active power management and inverters' is 'not something so far that we have done or that we have done in any meaningful way' — adjacencies must stay true to the interconnect strategy.

CEO Adam Norwitt on supply: Amphenol has 150 operations, each run by a general manager, and no central procurement organization; general managers make internal investments ahead of expected demand and create 'a multiplicity of sources for those things that maybe the vendors couldn't keep up with'; 'we don't see any significant bottlenecks' affecting Q2 results or the guidance for Q3 and beyond. On industrial: instrumentation is growing very strongly ('Not surprising given factories and the build-out of semiconductors'), as are factory automation, electrification, battery storage, heavy equipment, alternative energy and safety. In mobile devices Amphenol has been a hinge manufacturer for 'more than two decades.'
